{{Short description|French scientist}}
[[File:Denis Gratias.jpg|thumb|Denis Gratias]]
'''Denis Gratias''', born on 22 September 1947 in Paris (France) is a French scientist, emeritus research director at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]]. His speciality is materials science, in particular [[crystallography]]. Since the discovery of [[quasicrystal]]s by [[Dan Shechtman]] in 1982, he has contributed to their description, notably by developing theoretical models. He is a correspondent member at the [[French Academy of Sciences]] since 1994.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Liste-des-membres-de-l-Academie-des-sciences-/-G/denis-gratias.html|title=Académie des sciences|last=|first=|date=|website=|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160604205009/http://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Liste-des-membres-de-l-Academie-des-sciences-/-G/denis-gratias.html |archive-date=2016-06-04 |access-date=}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Denis Gratias graduated as a chemical engineer in 1970 at [[Chimie ParisTech]]. In 1978, Denis Gratias defended his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] thesis at the Structural Metallurgy Laboratory (CNRS-ENSCP), entitled "Crystallography of interfaces in homogeneous crystals"<ref>{{cite thesis|title=CRISTALLOGRAPHIE DES INTERFACES DANS LES CRISTAUX HOMOGENES / DENIS GRATIAS - Sudoc|url=https://www.sudoc.fr/042491134|website=www.sudoc.fr|date=1979 |access-date=2020-01-07|publication-date= |last1=Gratias |first1=Denis }}</ref> and developed with Richard Portier a formalism of fast electron diffraction.<ref>D. Gratias and R. Portier, Time-like perturbation method in high-energy electron diffraction, Acta Crystallogr. A, 39 4, 576-584 (1983).</ref> He then completed his post-doctoral training at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] where he was interested in the problems of statistical [[thermodynamics]] of generalized mean field<ref>J. M. Sanchez, F. Ducastelle and D. Gratias, Generalized cluster description of multicomponent systems, Physica A, 128(1-2), 334-350 (1984)</ref> (Cluster Variation Method).

Back in France, he took up his position at the Centre d'Études de Chimie Métallurgique (CECM), [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] laboratory in [[Vitry-sur-Seine]] (France), but was soon invited by [[John W. Cahn|John-Werner Cahn]] to the Institute of Theoretical Physics at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara|University of California]] at [[Santa Barbara, California|Santa Barbara]] (USA) to participate in an interdisciplinary collaboration on theoretical physics and materials science. It was on this occasion that he was confronted with the unresolved problem of the 5th-order diffraction observed in April 1982 by Dan Shechtman. He contributed to the seminal paper<ref>D. Shechtman, I. Blech, D. Gratias and J. W. Cahn, Metallic phase with long-range orientational order and no translational symmetry, Phy.Rev. Lett. 53 (20), 1951-1953 (1984)</ref> of 1984 announcing the discovery of quasicrystals.

Upon his return, a long period of intense collaboration on crystallography began between the CECM at Vitry and the Centre de physique théorique (CPHT) of the [[École Polytechnique]] with Marianne Quiquandon, André Katz and Michel Duneau.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Denis Gratias, professeur à Chimie ParisTech, élu à l'Académie des sciences |url=https://www.chimieparistech.psl.eu/ecole/actualites/denis-gratias-professeur-a-chimie-paristech-elu-a-lacademie-des-sciences-des/ |access-date=2023-10-14 |website=Chimie ParisTech - PSL |language=fr-FR}}</ref>

In 2000, Denis Gratias and his wife [[Marianne Quiquandon]] moved to [[Châtillon, Hauts-de-Seine|Châtillon]] to the Laboratoire d'étude des microstructures (LEM [archive], a joint ONERA-CNRS laboratory), which he directed until 2009.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2011-10-05 |title=At ONERA, a CNRS researcher involved with the Nobel Prize for Chemistry 2011 |url=https://www.onera.fr/en/news/at-onera-a-cnrs-researcher-involved-with-the-nobel-prize-for-chemistry-2011 |access-date=2023-10-14 |website=www.onera.fr |language=fr-FR}}</ref>

Since 2014, he has been CNRS Emeritus Research Director assigned to Chimie ParisTech, at the Institut de Recherche de Chimie Paris (IRCP), within the structural metallurgy team.<ref name=":0" />

== Teaching ==
*    1991 to 2002: Lecturer at the Ecole Polytechnique (Physics of Materials, Small Classes of Quantum Mechanics)<ref name=":0" />
*    1997 to 2006: Professor in charge of the Quantum Physics course at the [[Chimie ParisTech|Ecole Nationale Supérieure de Chimie de Paris]] (ENSCP).<ref name=":0" />
